english.title: Breach a Female Genital Mutilation protection order
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, **(..SPECIFY THE ACT/OMISSION PERFORMED..) which you were prohibited from doing by an FGM protection order made on **(..SPECIFY DATE ORDER WAS MADE..) by **(..SPECIFY COURT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraphs 4(1) and 4(5) of Schedule 2 to the Female Genital Mutilation Act 2003.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
without reasonable excuse
did anything prohibited by an FGM protection order

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) In the case of an FGM protection order made by virtue of paragraph 5(1) of Schedule 2, a person can be guilty of this offence only in respect of conduct engaged in at a time when the person was aware of the existence of the order
(ii) Where a person is convicted of this offence in respect of any conduct, the conduct is not punishable as a contempt of court.
(iii) A person cannot be convicted of this offence in respect of any conduct which has been punished as a contempt of court.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/ 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see paragraph 4(5)(b) of Schedule 2 to the Female Genital Mutilation Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time Limit For Prosecutions
None
